clue.text: News learned in the officers' dining-room

definitions.text: News learned in the officers' dining-room

parts.words: News learned in the officers' dining-room
parts.note: a cryptic picture of word of what is going on, picked up in the military mess where officers eat, read as what the mess passes on

explanation.surface: An officer catches up on the latest gossip over dinner in the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The officers' dining-room is the mess, so the clue hints at what is heard there; the whole clue describes the answer playfully rather than building it from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Communications passed from one person to another are the news someone receives.

clue.text: Decorative work done bit by bit

definitions.text: Decorative work done bit by bit

parts.words: Decorative work done bit by bit
parts.note: literally a picture built from small pieces of tile or glass set one at a time, but it reads as any slow, piecemeal job

explanation.surface: Some ornamental craftwork is finished slowly, a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: This art form assembles small tesserae into a picture, piece by piece.

clue.text: Attitude taken by 10, quite wrongly

indicators.note: the letters of the other answer are put together quite wrongly, that is in a fresh order

parts.note: 10 refers to the answer at 10 across, ASCENT

explanation.surface: Someone's point of view is badly mistaken, judged against another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite wrongly' rearranges the letters of the answer to 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or point of view adopted on some matter.

clue.text: Confused tot with a foreign article

parts.note: to tot up is to add
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A muddled child is paired with an article from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child, but here it is the verb, as in totting up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective this means muddled, as in an addle-headed thinker.

clue.text: Oriental egghead getting behind

indicators.note: the head of the word egg is its opening letter

parts.note: astern is a nautical word for behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An Asian intellectual is falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' tempts as an intellectual; split it as 'egg' plus 'head', meaning its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things from the East, particularly Asia.

clue.text: American lawyer backing evil counsel

indicators.note: backing means the lawyer's letters are turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
vice is wickedness

explanation.surface: A US attorney supports wicked guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns DA into AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel and this word both mean guidance offered to someone.

clue.text: Pay five hundred is the order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
taken as written
a charge is an order or instruction, as a judge's charge

explanation.surface: Paying out a large sum is what has been commanded.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a debt is to settle it in full.

clue.text: It's about time, note, for repeats

indicators.note: the word it's goes about, that is around, the other pieces

parts.note: taken as its letters without the apostrophe
an era is a period of time
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone insists, again and again, that the moment has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ERA plus TE inside IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean says or does something over and over.

clue.text: An admission about making tea appeal

indicators.note: the word for admission is placed about, that is around, the reworked tea

parts.note: entry is admission, the right to go in

indicators.note: making suggests the letters of tea are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone confesses while brewing a pot, pleading for sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges TEA into EAT, and 'about' puts that inside ENTRY; 'An' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or request.

clue.text: Hit and run, being negligent

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver is plainly careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit and run' reads as a road crime, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless, hasty work done without proper attention is described this way.

clue.text: 2 may well get a rise

indicators.note: the other answer may well get a new order of letters to give this one

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer at 2 down, STANCE

explanation.surface: A second item could well lead to an increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well get' rearranges the letters of the answer to 2 down; 2 and 10 are anagrams of each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up or climbing, such as of a hill, is a rise.

clue.text: Irritation caused by copper leaving field

indicators.note: the coin leaving means its letter is taken away

parts.note: a pitch is a sports field
P is a penny, a copper coin in British money

explanation.surface: A police officer is annoyed at being sent off the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman; here it is a penny, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tickling skin irritation, or figuratively a restless desire.

clue.text: Popular bond — about right for that extra cash

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the word for bond goes about, that is around, the letter for right

parts.note: cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: A well-liked investment bond gives about the right amount of extra money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bond' looks financial, but it is CEMENT, which bonds bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an addition, especially a rise in salary.

clue.text: Swell central Winchester street

indicators.note: central takes the middle pair from the ten-letter city name

parts.note: Ave is short for avenue, a street

explanation.surface: A fine thoroughfare runs through the middle of Winchester, an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an adjective meaning fine; it is the rise and fall of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhythmic rising of the sea, or a lifting surge, is a swell.

clue.text: Royalty in this country

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: The monarch is at home in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair for an Irish reader or as a patriotic phrase: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic name for Ireland, a nation addressed as one's homeland.

clue.text: Checks taxes-not for the first time!

parts.note: re- means again, so something done not for the first time
to tax is to strain, as tax one's patience

explanation.surface: Someone complains that duties are being inspected once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxes' looks like a noun, levies; it is the verb, puts a strain on.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or curb.

clue.text: Spinning threads is most difficult

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters turning into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning yarn is the toughest job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' rearranges THREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the superlative of tough, meaning the most demanding.

clue.text: A fan sees a single act following

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to do is to act
later means afterwards, following on

explanation.surface: A supporter watches a solo performance afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of idols, figuratively an adoring admirer.

clue.text: Civil spoken when put under =the heartless politician

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece put under another comes after it
heartless removes the middle letter of the word the

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Polite speech is placed beneath a cold-hearted MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when put under' places ORAL after TE (from 'the heartless') plus MP. The stray '=' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means secular, of worldly affairs rather than the Church, as civil law against canon law.

clue.text: Topping investment for women!

parts.note: investment here is clothing one is invested in, and topping hints at fine outer garments, not a great financial deal

explanation.surface: A tip for a first-rate investment aimed at women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' suggests money, but it is the older sense of what one is invested, that is clothed, in.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's frocks are garments one is clad in, an old sense of investment.

clue.text: Some humane purchaser freeing a slave

indicators.note: some of the letters from the words that follow give the answer

explanation.surface: A kind buyer liberates a slave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the letters at the end of 'purchaser' and the start of 'freeing'; 'humane' is only scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land, effectively unfree.

clue.text: Plant a large number and it will be regretted

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: Planting a great many will be something to regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb, sow; it is the herb rue.
explanation.definitionFit: To have felt sorrow about something done is to have regretted it.

clue.text: Carry on and run into an attendant

parts.note: to ram is to run into
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: Keep going and bump into a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' is the definition in its sense of behave wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, to carry on in a wild manner.

clue.text: Hear sterling is to catch up

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for catch is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Someone hears the pound is recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention with the ears, to hear.

clue.text: Undertaking transport provision

parts.note: undertaking reads as a business venture but means the work of funeral directors, so this is their vehicle

explanation.surface: A company is set up to supply transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaking' means the business of an undertaker, not just any project.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral car carries the coffin, the vehicle undertakers supply.

clue.text: See through a fast mover

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
per means through or by means of

explanation.surface: Watch a quick runner go past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See through' looks like a phrasal verb, but it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lopes, running with long easy strides.

clue.text: Forgiving and touching letter

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A moving letter offering forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like moving; it is 'regarding', RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remissive means pardoning, from remission of sins.

clue.text: Seeing sense

definitions.meaning: one of the five bodily faculties

explanation.surface: Sight is the faculty of seeing and one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is both the act of seeing and one of the five bodily faculties.

clue.text: Move to capture sanctimonious criminal

indicators.note: the word for move goes round, as if capturing, the word for sanctimonious

parts.note: to turn is to move round
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Police manoeuvre to catch a self-righteous crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was a famous 18th-century English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Turpin was a notorious highwayman hanged at York in 1739.

clue.text: Present mirth hath present "Shakespeare (Twelfth Night)

parts.note: a quotation with its last word missing, from a song in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night: the solver supplies the word that completes the line

explanation.surface: A line from Feste's song in Twelfth Night with its last word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is from the song 'O mistress mine': solvers fill in the gap from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth naturally produces chuckling, the word completing the quoted line.

clue.text: A portion of mackerel is healthy and appetising food

indicators.note: A portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some oily fish is a healthy and tasty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition began with 'and', which is a link word joining wordplay to definition, so the definition is just 'appetising food'.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a tasty condiment or savoury that whets the appetite.

clue.text: The condemnation of "X" in terrible scene

indicators.note: the number goes in, inside, the jumbled letters
terrible suggests the letters of scene are badly mangled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A dreadful episode in which someone marked X is condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges SCENE into SENCE, and 'in' puts TEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's sentence is the formal condemnation of a convicted person.
